cold-open.title: Emergency hospital during Influenza epidemic, Camp Funston, Kansas - NCP 1603
cold-open.description:
Emergency hospital during influenza epidemic, Camp Funston, Kansas. 
Emergency hospital during influenza epidemic (NCP 1603), National Museum of Health and Medicine.
Description: Beds with patients in an emergency hospital in Camp Funston, Kansas, in the midst of the influenza epidemic. The flu struck while America was at war, and was transported across the Atlantic on troop ships.
Date: circa 191
cold-open.credit:

kansas.title: George T. Desloge Reminiscences, Volume II, 1914-1919 - DPLA - cb5a17188120de0c3749eb1d62788dc4 (page 19)
kansas.description: George T. Desloge was a native of St. Louis, Missouri, who was born on November 5, 1880, into a very prominent family. He was in the National Guard of Missouri and a Veteran of the Spanish American War and WWI. In this original typescript two-volume book Desloge described his experiences as an instructor at the Officers Training Camp at Ft. Riley, Kansas; Ft. Sheridan, Illinois; Camp Hancock, Geor
kansas.credit: Desloge, George Thatcher, 1880-1943, This file was contributed to Wikimedia Commons by Missouri Historical Society as part of a cooperation project. The donation was facilitated by the Digital Public

second-wave.title: SpanishFluWardWalterReed
second-wave.description:
"Walter Reed Hospital Flu Ward". 

Photo of Walter Reed Hospital, Washington, D.C., during the great Influenza Pandemic of 1918 - 1919, also known as the "Spanish Flu".  Patients are set up in rows of beds on an open gallery, seperated by hung sheets.  A nurse wears a cloth mask over her nose and mouth.
second-wave.date: Not dated, probably during the height of the epidemic, 1918 - 1919
second-wave.credit: Harris & Ewing photographers, Photo by Harris & Ewing via Library of Congress website at [1]; converted from TIFF to .jpg and border cropped before upload
